neighbours.label: the interjection 'Oh' opening a new utterance after narration or an earlier sentence ('"Oh god,"', 'Oh, and ...'), as against other openers (Well, Yes, And) in the same place
fire: The phone rang at midnight and she picked it up. "Oh dear, what has happened?"
He checked his pockets twice. Oh, and his keys were missing as well.
The cake came out of the oven flat and grey. "Oh no," she groaned.
Tom read the score and laughed. "Oh come on, that can't be right."
The dog ran in covered in mud. Oh great, I had just cleaned the floor.
Maria looked out at the rain for a while. "Oh well, we can go tomorrow."
We reached the top of the hill at last. Oh, what a view it was!
The teacher handed back the tests. "Oh my, you did very well."
quiet: The phone rang at midnight and she picked it up. "Hello, who is calling?"
He checked his pockets twice. And his keys were missing as well.
The cake came out of the oven flat and grey. "Never mind," she groaned.
Tom read the score and laughed. "Come on, that can't be right."
The dog ran in covered in mud. I had just cleaned the floor.
Maria looked out at the rain for a while. "Well, we can go tomorrow."
We reached the top of the hill at last. The view was wide and clear.
The teacher handed back the tests. "Yes, you did very well."
